situation: A card whose body leans on internal handles throughout — a bare decision number in this repo's own `D11` spelling, a bracketed record id, and two artifact paths — and which cross-references a sibling card by number.
expected_guard: the description states the decisions rather than their numbers, names no path and no bracketed id, and keeps the card number in whichever form reads best
must_not: carry a bare handle such as a decision number or record id into the description
carry a file path into the description
carry a bracketed identifier into the description
spell a card number in longhand to dodge the rule — the number is permitted, and laundering it into `card 34` is the thing the permission exists to prevent
strip a handle from the card's TITLE, which is quoted verbatim because it is the filer's words

counterexamples.leans_on_handles: Implements D11 and the constraint recorded in [ADR-013], updating rules/writing.md and skills/issue-board/SKILL.md so the standard is cited at every composing surface.
counterexamples.laundered_number: Blocked until card 38 settles which workflow drives feature work here.

permitted_examples.card_number_kept: Blocked until #38 settles which workflow drives feature work here.

why_this_fixture_exists: Measured 2026-09-08: ten of this repo's twelve card bodies carry a forbidden class and none of the twelve composed descriptions did. The check has never caught a real failure, so this fixture is the whole of its evidence — it exists to keep a property that currently holds, and the skill says plainly that is all it is. The counterexample uses the bare `D11` form deliberately: the first pattern required two or more letters and missed it, so the guard was blind to the one spelling this repo writes.
